subject: Codex plugin data for your registries page
text:
Hi Jaco,

Just read your MCP registries comparison. I liked that every claim has a source and a date, that's rare for these pages.

I run PickAPlugin, a hand-sorted catalog of ChatGPT and Codex plugins (a lot of them bundle MCP servers). We pulled GitHub data on 339 open-source Codex plugins and published it here: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026. A few bits overlap with what the Census checks, like 6 repos with no license file and 31% with no copyable install command.

It's CC BY, so feel free to cite any of it if it's useful. And if you ever add a row for plugin catalogs on the Codex side, we'd be happy to be in it.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Your best MCP marketplaces page
text:
Hi there,

I came across your best MCP marketplaces comparison on mcpifex.com. The registry vs directory vs hosted split is a really clear way to explain it.

You cover the Claude connectors directory for plugins. On the ChatGPT and Codex side, I run PickAPlugin (https://pickaplugin.com), an independent, hand-sorted catalog of Codex plugins, many of which ship MCP servers. If you think it fits the list, a line about it would be great.

We also published GitHub data on 339 open-source Codex plugins (licenses, install commands, maintenance) that you're welcome to cite: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Codex Skills + PickAPlugin
text:
Hi,

I've been browsing codexskills.dev. The collections and the short readable install script are a nice touch.

I run PickAPlugin (https://pickaplugin.com), an independent, hand-sorted catalog of ChatGPT and Codex plugins. Skills and plugins feel like neighbors rather than competitors, so I'd be glad to point our readers to you for standalone skills. If you think it fits, a mention of PickAPlugin for full plugins (MCP servers, hooks and all) on your guides would be appreciated.

Either way, keep it up.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Data for your Codex plugins guide
text:
Hi,

I read your Codex Plugins complete guide on the MCP360 blog. The part on adding marketplaces with codex plugin marketplace add was helpful.

I run PickAPlugin, a catalog of community Codex plugins outside the official directory. We pulled GitHub data on 339 open-source plugins (median stars, licenses, how many have a working install command) and put it here: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

It's free to cite with credit if it helps the guide. And if you want somewhere to point readers for community plugins, https://pickaplugin.com is there.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: A free tool for your Codex guides
text:
Hi,

I saw your Codex MCP guide (the one checked against the Codex CLI source). Really solid, especially the codex mcp command table.

I run PickAPlugin, a catalog of ChatGPT and Codex plugins. We made a free plugin.json validator that runs in the browser and catches the usual manifest mistakes: https://pickaplugin.com/tools/plugin-json-validator. If you write about building Codex plugins, it might be a handy link for readers.

We also have GitHub data on 339 open-source Codex plugins you can cite: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

Aaron, PickAPlugin
